If \(f:M\to N\) is piecewise smooth between piecewise smooth Riemannian manifolds, the \(k\)-dilation of \(f\), denoted \(\Dil_k(f)\), is the infimal \(\Lambda\) such that for every \(k\)-dimensional submanifold \(\Sigma\subset M\),
\[
\Vol_k(f(\Sigma))\le \Lambda \Vol_k(\Sigma).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\Dil_k(f)=\sup_{x\in M}\|\Lambda^k df\|.
\]
Let \(R\subset \mathbb R^4\) be a \(4\)-dimensional rectangle with side lengths \(R_1\le R_2\le R_3\le R_4\).
Let \(S\subset \mathbb R^4\) be a \(4\)-dimensional rectangle with side lengths \(S_1\le S_2\le S_3\le S_4\).
Let \(f:(R,\partial R)\to(S,\partial S)\) be piecewise smooth, of degree \(1\), and satisfy \(\Dil_2(f)\le 1\).
There exists a universal constant \(k>0\) such that, if \(R_1\le kS_1\), then either
\[
R_3R_4>kS_3S_4,
\]
or
\[
R_1R_2R_3R_4>kS_1S_2^{1/2}S_3^{3/2}S_4.
\]
